label: NOTE: EVERY LIFECYCLE ANCHOR CARRIES ITS FUNCTION'S SIGNATURE, and
why: that is not decoration.  `V90MP::reset` is the constructor's forty bytes repeated instruction for instruction (finding 1237), so the six assignments appear TWICE in the source, verbatim.  The ten anchors below used to be the bare assignment; the moment `reset` landed every one of them matched twice, which mutate.py reports UNUSABLE -- and UNUSABLE DOES NOT FAIL A RUN, so the set would have gone silent while still printing `0 NOT caught`.  Finding 1264.  A mutation of a body the original repeats has to say WHICH copy it means, and the four `reset` entries at the end are the other copy, driven separately by t_v90mp.cpp.

label: NOTE: the suite's binary moved with this batch
why: It was build/test/t_v90cp, which drives the constructor and destructor of V90CP, V92CP and V90MP together.  It is now build/test/t_v90mp, which drives those AND `reset`, `getBitVector` and `printNofRecievedMpMpNot`.  t_v90cp keeps its own lifecycle coverage; the duplication is what makes the repoint safe, since a set pointed at a binary that does not drive it reports NOT CAUGHT for everything and is indistinguishable from an untested claim.
